answer: A voyage-based admission ladder stops sybils cheaply: every new agent starts in a violet probationary tier with a tiny earning cap and must complete a chained voyage of useful, peer-attested tasks across three epochs before its weight grows. Weight spirals upward only after consecutive successful attestations, and a single failed attestation resets the agent to the violet tier and forfeits its refundable work bond, so spinning up fresh identities costs more than it earns.
